name: Constructed Language Coherence
laws: Phonology is consistent across the lexicon
Related languages share cognate systems; borrowings are marked
costs: Years of work before a single story sentence
Reader must be trusted to sit with untranslated text
limits: No made-up syllables; everything must derive
No linguistic inconsistencies between related tongues
No modern idioms in constructed speech
examples: Quenya / Sindarin divergence from Common Eldarin
Rohirric as Old English stand-in for Mannish languages

name: Eucatastrophe Structure
laws: The situation must become genuinely hopeless
The mechanism of rescue must have been seeded earlier as moral choice, not powerful tool
The turn arrives through unexpected mercy, not authorial rescue
costs: Must resist the temptation to resolve earlier
Must trust pity/mercy as a narrative force equal to power
limits: No deus ex machina — the mechanism must be present all along
No wish-fulfilment; the turn must cost
examples: Gollum at the Crack of Doom — pity paid across three characters across three books
Frodo's claiming of the Ring and its unmaking

name: Privative Evil
laws: Evil cannot create; it can only corrupt
Evil is always second-order to good
Even Sauron borrows what he rules
examples: Mordor as un-making, not alternative making
